proof_system_scope: Cook-Reckhow propositional proof systems (or equivalent polynomial-time verifiable refutation systems for UNSAT)

theorem.name: P_BOUNDED_PLUS_POLYTIME_AUTOMATIZABLE_IFF_P_EQUALS_NP_EXISTS
theorem.statement: There exists a Cook-Reckhow proof system that is both polynomially bounded and polynomial-time automatizable if and only if P=NP.
forward_direction: Let Psys be polynomially bounded: every tautology phi has a Psys-proof of size at most q(|phi|) for one fixed polynomial q.
Let Psys be polynomial-time automatizable in the standard shortest-proof sense: on a tautology phi it outputs a Psys-proof in time polynomial in |phi| plus the length of a shortest Psys-proof.
By polynomial boundedness, the shortest proof length is at most q(|phi|), so the automatizer runs in polynomial time in |phi|.

Thus TAUT is decidable in deterministic polynomial time: run the automatizer with its totality/acceptance convention and verify the returned proof; equivalently use the corresponding refutation formulation for UNSAT.
Since TAUT is coNP-complete and P is closed under complement, TAUT in P implies SAT in P, hence P=NP.
reverse_direction: Assume P=NP. Then TAUT is in P because P=coP and NP=coNP=P.

Define a Cook-Reckhow system whose proof of a tautology phi can be phi itself, with the proof-system function checking tautologicity in polynomial time and outputting phi when valid (and a fixed tautology otherwise).
This system is polynomially bounded because proof length is O(|phi|).
It is polynomial-time automatizable because on tautological input the automatizer outputs phi itself.
Therefore such a proof system exists.

relation_to_known_results.cook_reckhow: Cook-Reckhow: a polynomially bounded propositional proof system exists iff NP=coNP.
relation_to_known_results.new_TRUMP_use: Adding polynomial-time proof discovery to polynomial boundedness raises the requirement from NP=coNP-level short-proof existence to P=NP-level uniform discovery.
sources: Stephen A. Cook and Robert A. Reckhow, The relative efficiency of propositional proof systems, JSL 44(1), 1979
standard automatizability definition: output a proof in time polynomial in formula size and shortest-proof length

derived_TRUMP_consequence.claim: TRUMP should not enumerate stronger proof languages hoping that proof-size strength alone will eventually discharge L3. For any Cook-Reckhow route, the combination needed for universal polynomial-size evidence plus generic polynomial-time discovery is already equivalent to the final P=NP target.
what_remains_legitimate: prove polynomial discovery for a specifically restricted exact class and clearly keep its scope local
prove a search-hardness barrier for a fixed proof language
prove a new structural theorem that avoids requiring p-bounded proof search for arbitrary instances
find a genuinely different decision architecture whose polynomial runtime is proved directly rather than inferred from short-proof existence

dead_zone_epistemic_mapping.forbidden: Search failure may not be collapsed into UNSAT, SAT, nonexistence of a proof, or impossibility of polynomial discovery.

next_rule: Do not choose another proof language merely because it is stronger. A next route must state exactly which assumption of this meta-barrier it avoids or discharge L3 by a direct polynomial-time theorem.
